children.value: > Fact From Story When you see a total, such as 210.5 in a basketball game, it represents the combined score anticipated from both teams.
> > Fact From Story If you believe the actual combined score will surpass this number, you'd bet on the "over." Conversely, if you think it will be less, you'd choose the "under."
> > > Fact From Story Bookmakers set a predicted total score for the game, and bettors choose whether they think the actual combined score will surpass (over) or fall short of (under) that number.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge An anticipated combined score is a prediction of what the final score will be.
> > Fact From Story Beside this number, you'll typically find "over" and "under" options.
> > > Fact From Story Conversely, if you think it will be less, you'd choose the "under."
> > > Fact From Story If you believe the actual combined score will surpass this number, you'd bet on the "over."
> > > Commonsense Knowledge Every betting choice is a prediction.
> > Commonsense Knowledge The "over" and "under" options describe a range of possible outcomes.
> Commonsense Knowledge To understand a wager, one must understand the terms and numbers involved.
